text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — API_GATEWAY_5XX_RATE spike detected for hosted-inference (region: us-west-2). 5m error rate 6.8% (SLO 1%). Alerting oncall team.

alex: seeing it too. dashboard shows 502/504s from gateway here. any recent deploys?

maya: no deploys in last 2 hours from releases channel. can someone paste the query that raised it?

oncall-bot: Query: `sum(rate(http_responses_total{service="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="api-gateway"}[5m]))` returned 0.068.

ben: adding traces — jaeger shows requests timing out at the egress to model-worker-pool. spans end with `connection reset` or `upstream timeout`.

sam: repro steps from a dev machine: hitting the inference endpoint with a steady 50rps small payloads yields intermittent 502 after ~200ms, full response sometimes 7-12s then 502.

alex: can we check connection saturation on the pool? `kubectl top pod`?

maya: running k8s metrics, noticed worker pods in nodepool-a have 90-95% network TX, CPU low. kernel drops rising.

ben: log snippet from gateway: ```
2026-07-12T14:21:03Z gateway ERROR upstream request failed: read: connection reset by peer
2026-07-12T14:21:03Z gateway WARN routing to fallback model-quantized-v2
```

oncall-bot: Noted automatic fallback to quantized variant triggered 120 times in the last 10m.

alex: that fallback is masking some errors but increasing latency — explains the customer complaints. We need to stop routing to overloaded nodepool. Can we mark nodepool-a drained?

maya: starting cordon/drain for nodepool-a. `kubectl cordon node XXX && kubectl drain node XXX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — doing it one node at a time.

sam: telemetry shows request queue at gateway spiking: `nginx_upstream_queue_length{pool="nodepool-a"}` > 300. we should throttle routing to that pool.

ben: temporarily adjusting smart-routing weight: set weight(nodepool-a)=0 in routing service config. patch: ```
PATCH /routing/weights
{ "nodepool-a": 0 }
```

alex: applied. traffic now migrates to nodepool-b and dedicated-pool. error rate dropping to 1.2% after 3m. still above SLO but trending.

maya: investigating root cause: kernel networking bug or NIC driver on nodepool-a instances (same instance type and age). support ticket created with cloud provider (ticket #CP-98721).

obs-bot: Observability note: Tracing gaps detected — ~12% of spans missing KV cache spans during spike. Possible tracer sampling or SDK timeout upstream.

ben: interesting — the worker processes were OOM-killed earlier today but restarted. could be ephemeral resource contention causing connections to reset. need to confirm pod restart counts: `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}\n'`.

sam: restart counts for nodepool-a workers: 3-7 in last 24h. nodepool-b 0-1.

alex: action list: 1) keep weight=0 for nodepool-a until provider responds, 2) increase probe timeouts on gateway to avoid premature resets: set `upstream_read_timeout=15s` temporarily, 3) add alert for upstream_queue_length > 200, 4) schedule post-incident debug for kernel/NIC.

maya: applied upstream timeout change and alert. documenting commands in runbook.

oncall-bot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV2, started=1812345678, mitigated=1812345880, owners=[alex,maya,ben].

ben: confirmed error rate back to 0.6% after routing change and node drains. starting a controlled canary to move small % back to nodepool-a once provider confirms.

sam: customer support notes: opened ticket with affected customers, provided temporary mitigation details and ETA for root cause. cc: support-eng.

alex: follow-ups: (a) add more robust connection pooling and retry backpressure in gateway, (b) analyze restart cause for workers, (c) add probe across entire RPC path not just gateway healthcheck, (d) improve tracing sampling to catch KV cache operations.

maya: will own (b) and (c). ben + obs team will own (a) and (d). putting a postmortem on calendar tomorrow.

alex: thanks team. we'll update here once cloud provider responds. :thumbsup:
